summary: Sadajiro Sugiura worked in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania (PhD), and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, where he became professor emeritus.

Saerji is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held positions at Peking University, serving as an associate professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Sai Susarla works in computational studies and Indology. He served as dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).

Said Reza Huseini specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2011–2014), King's College London (~2014–2015), and Leiden University (~2017–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib. He held posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and was a reader at Australian National University (1967–1986).
Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MPhil at Cardiff University under Max Deeg and Peter Harvey, and is attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.
Sakunoshin Motoda was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kenyon College, the University of Pennsylvania, and Columbia University. He held a post at Rikkyo University from around 1907 to 1923.
Sakutaro Fujioka worked in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1894 to 1897 and held a post there from around 1900 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar and abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017. He studied under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, founded the Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and taught numerous students.

Sakyong Mipham works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded. He served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed her studies at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and served as professor and professor emerita at James Madison University (~1992–2017).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman works in Indology and linguistics. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri, and served at UC Berkeley, becoming Senior Lecturer Emerita.
Sally McAra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she studied under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

Sally Mellick Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996–1997).

Salomon Lefmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Münster, Berlin (PhD under Franz Bopp), Heidelberg, and Paris. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University starting in 1866, becoming an associate and later honorary professor.

Saloni Mathur is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. She serves at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was an associate professor of art history and later professor and chair of the Department of Art History.

Sam van Schaik is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Manchester. He has held positions at SOAS University of London and the British Library as Head of the Endangered Archives Programme.
Samani Pratibha Pragya works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she was attested as a research assistant in 2020.
Sambhavi Ganesh is a scholar in Indology. Attested in 2026, she is a doctoral student at the University of Edinburgh studying under supervisor Radhika Govinda.

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti specializes in Indology and religious studies. He has held posts at the University of Calcutta and at The Asiatic Society, where he is attested in 2026 as Professor (Special Invitee).
